title: Playing by number and funeral music requests
summary: Dejan explains that old brass bands such as Imperial, Red Allen and Tuxedo played from numbered sheet music and would not hire non-readers. His band now knows the numbers by heart, though he brings music for special funeral requests, and he loves playing funeral dirges.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: And like right now it seems most of the street bands, most of the bands play, I mean you know, like, without sheet music, whereas they used to play sheet music and by number.

Yeah, well you see, the by number thing which you're talking about, you see years ago the older musicians, you know like they had some good brass bands years ago when I was a kid, like the Imperial Brass Band, and they had and they had and Red Allen Brass Band from Across the River, the Tuxedo Brass Band with Celestan, or they had some fine brass bands, and they all had music. And if they hire a man to play in a band, what they used to do, put the name of the piece of music off and use the number. Them that didn't have a number, they put a number on it and say, let's play such and such a number. And if you could, well, if you didn't hear you, they know you wouldn't read that music, they don't hire no more. So that's the way it was. Because all the good brass bands, I would say the good ones, because they had a couple other brass bands that were just going on and playing, you know, but the good brass bands. Well now you see, we play these numbers so many times and so often we don't need the music for it ourselves, you know. Only the time I pull music out for the band, it's like, oh sometimes we play a big funeral and I want to play, you know, so you might ask for a request. Like if Larry Bernstein around him is special, he can ask for West Long. So I usually carry that with me when he's going to be around, you know. Or a couple others, you know, like Flea as a Boyd or something like that, according to how long the funeral is, so you add some of these beautiful, pretty music in it, you know, because I think all the funeral drives are so beautiful. Yeah. Yeah, I do. That's why I love to play the funeral. And if you pay attention to me when I'm playing the funeral, you'll see some tears rolling down my cheeks, you know.
